title: Associate AI Applications Engineer II
location: North Chicago, IL, US
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
As an Associate AI Applications Engineer II, you will design, build, and deploy interactive user interfaces and web applications that enable users to explore, evaluate, and work with machine learning and AI models. You will translate models and data science outputs into intuitive, reliable, and scalable applications, and support the review and validation of ML/AI-enabled apps, under the direction of a more senior leader. You will demonstrate strong front-end and full-stack engineering skills and a working understanding of ML/AI model lifecycles, APIs, and data integration.
Responsibilities:
Design and develop dynamic, interactive user interfaces and applications (e.g., Streamlit, Gradio, Dash, React) that expose ML and AI models, including generative AI and agent-based solutions, to business and scientific users.
Integrate applications with model endpoints, APIs, and data sources, enabling real-time inference, parameter controls, visualization of results, and user feedback capture.
Collaborate with data scientists and ML engineers to turn prototypes and models into production-ready, maintainable applications.
Review ML/AI-enabled applications for functionality, usability, performance, security, and responsible AI considerations, and provide clear, actionable feedback.
Write, test, and maintain high-quality code using version control, code review, and CI/CD practices; troubleshoot and resolve application defects.
Gather user requirements and iterate on designs through demos, user testing, and feedback to improve usability and adoption.
Deploy and monitor applications on cloud and container platforms, ensuring reliability, scalability, and appropriate logging and observability.
Document application architecture, APIs, and user guides, and contribute to reusable components and standards for AI application development.
Learn and evaluate new frameworks, AI tools, and technologies, and recommend improvements to our application development approach.
Understand and adhere to corporate standards regarding applicable Corporate and Divisional Policies, including code of conduct, safety, GxP compliance, and data security.
Required:
Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Science, or a related field with 2 years of experience; or Master’s Degree with no additional experience.
Respective years of relevant experience developing software or web applications.
Proficiency in Python and backends like FastAPI.
Proficiency in Python and JavaScript/TypeScript; experience with React, or similar.
Experience building applications that consume ML/AI models via REST APIs or SDKs
Familiarity with ML concepts and tools (e.g., scikit-learn, PyTorch, MLflow) and generative AI/LLM application patterns.
Working knowledge of cloud platforms (e.g., AWS, Azure), containers, Git, and CI/CD
Strong data visualization and UX design sensibility.
Strong communication skills and ability to collaborate with technical and non-technical partners
Preferred:
Experience in life sciences or regulated (GxP) environments.
2 or more years of experience developing software or web applications preferred.

As defined in the scope of the assigned development project(s), the Medical Director, Clinical Development will have global responsibilities and fulfill the following roles:
Therapeutic Area Medical Director (TAMD)
With supervision, the Medical Director oversees the planning, execution and interpretation of clinical trials or research activities of a clinical development program. The TAMD participates in cross-functional teams to generate, deliver, and interpret high-quality clinical data supporting overall product medical, scientific and business strategy, all while providing mentorship and guidance to junior team members where needed.
The TAMD may be asked to participate in internal process improvement activities within R&D and the wider organization, as well as external interactions with KOLs and Regulatory authorities.
The employee must conduct their work activities in compliance with all relevant laws, regulations, and regulatory guidelines as well as all AbbVie policies and procedures.
Note: While this job description is intended to be an accurate reflection of the job requirements, management reserves the right to modify, add or remove duties from a particular job and to assign other duties as necessary and at any time.
The TAMD is responsible and accountable for the medical data management of clinical trials, according to applicable SOPs.  The TAMD supports the clinical studies in the Pipeline Commercialization Model, from early development to post-market, including life-cycle management. The TAMD fosters an atmosphere of collaboration, mutual respect, transparent communication, and data driven analyses according to the highest scientific standards and a focus on agility, efficiency and patient-centricity. The TAMD leads the responses for medical and scientific data questions, in collaboration with the TA-SD and other applicable functional and regional input. The TAMD responsibilities include:
With appropriate supervision, manages the design and implementation of study protocols for a clinical development program in support of the overall Product Development Plan, based on strong medical and scientific principles, knowledge of compliance and regulatory requirements, AbbVie’s customers, markets, business operations, and emerging issues. Oversees project-related education of investigators, study site personnel, and AbbVie study staff.
Has responsibility for medical oversight of clinical studies, monitoring overall study integrity, and review, interpretation, and communication of accumulating data pertaining to safety and efficacy of the product.  Along with Clinical Operations, is responsible for oversight of study enrollment and overall timelines for key deliverables.  Responsible for assessment and reporting of serious adverse events per corporate policy and regulations for those protocols on which assigned.
Safety-related responsibilities include but are not limited to: safety coding, safety narratives, overseeing ECG data where applicable, establishing lab alert values where appropriate, chairing and/or participating in a DMC when established for clinical trials, securing and participating in 24/7 medical coverage and checking voicemail for clinical study sites
Escalates relevant safety data review findings to the Product Safety Team
Contributes to design, analysis, interpretation, and reporting of scientific content of protocols, Investigator Brochures, Clinical Study Reports, regulatory submissions and responses, and other program documents.
Presents clinical trial data, especially safety data, related to clinical trials to internal and external stakeholders.
May serve on a Clinical Strategy Team as the clinical representative for the protocols for which the incumbent has responsibility.  Contributes to the development of a rigorous, cross-functionally-aligned, vetted Clinical Development Plan in collaboration with matrix team members.
Participates in opinion leader interactions related to the disease area(s); partners with Medical Affairs, Commercial and other functions in these activities as required, consistent with corporate policies.
Stays abreast of professional information and technology through conferences, medical literature, and other available training, to augment expertise in the therapeutic area.
Responsible for understanding the regulatory requirements related to the clinical studies and global drug/device development and accountable for complying with those requirements. May be asked to contribute to regulatory submissions, responses and discussions, as well as audits and inspections.
Ensures adherence to Good Clinical Practices, pharmacovigilance standards, standard operating procedures and to all other quality standards in conducting research.
Demonstrates initiative and participates in process improvement activities and other strategic or scientific initiatives/projects within R&D and the wider organization.
Medical degree (e.g., MD, DO, MBBS); scientific knowledge and experience in Aesthetics preferred. Completion of a residency program strongly preferred. Completion of a subspecialty fellowship is desirable.
Clinical trial experience in the pharmaceutical/device industry, academia, or equivalent is strongly preferred
Minimum 1 year of experience in medical monitoring of clinical trials an advantage
Ability to run a clinical research study with appropriate supervision
Strong desire and ability to collaborate in a cross-functional setting with different disciplines and across geographies
Knowledge of clinical trial methodology, regulatory and compliance requirements governing clinical trials and experience in the design of study protocols is desirable
Ability to interact externally and internally to support global scientific and business strategy
Track record of successful management of product safety matters (labeling negotiation, etc.) preferred
Experience in preparation of risk management plans, aggregate reports and company core safety information highly desirable
Sound judgment and experience in medical interpretation of safety findings for clinical trials

AWS Environmental is responsible for the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. • Coordinate with partner teams — including Construction, Design, Water, Legal, Real Estate, Power, and others — to manage construction and operational constraints.
• Develop site development strategies that are environmentally responsible and sustainable while meeting project timelines.

The AWS Environmental Team in AMER manages the environmental requirements during data center and infrastructure development in the Americas. We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

title: State Government Affairs Lead (Illinois)
location: Springfield, IL
description:
ABOUT BASE

Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As the first on-the-ground policy lead in Illinois, you will be the tactical architect of our regulatory and legislative strategy in the State, while at the same time prospecting opportunities in eastern RTOs more generally. You will serve as a high-impact advocate who can navigate the Illinois Commerce Commission (ICC) and the state legislature, while promoting our objectives with Illinois utilities and RTOs. You will bridge the gap between our innovative energy technology and the traditional utility landscape, ensuring that our tech and retail electricity solutions are not only compliant but actively shaping the future of the grid.



This will be a hybrid role between Austin and Chicago. At Base, our culture is the heartbeat of our success. We are a tight-knit team that thrives on the energy, spontaneous collaboration, and shared purpose that comes from working side-by-side in Austin. For this role, however, we recognize the unique need to be in Illinois. We will therefore look for a candidate who is committed to having a strong presence both in Austin and in Chicago. If based in Chicago, we will ask you to spend your first four to six weeks in Austin and then approximately one week per month thereafter.



What You’ll Do

 - Lead regulatory advocacy and ICC representation, participating in ICC proceedings, including rate cases, grid-modernization filings, and rulemakings, and becoming the principal point of contact for ICC Staff, Commissioners, and the Citizens Utility Board.

 - Guide the company’s advocacy in the implementation of recent Illinois legislation, SB25, and work with local officials to streamline AHJ requirements.

 - Draft and file petitions, testimonies, and comments that protect our market access and promote tech-forward utility regulations, while monitoring and ensuring company compliance with the Illinois Public Utilities Act and ICC administrative codes.

 - Manage the operational and strategic relationship with utilities and RTOs in Illinois, proactively identifying opportunities and risks, and representing the company in stakeholder proceedings.

 - Work with the broader policy team to develop our positioning in FERC proceedings relevant to our work in Illinois.

 - Act as an advocate for the company at the Illinois State Capitol, and monitor, analyze, and advocate for legislation that impacts our business.

 - Deploy data-driven arguments to persuade regulators and utility partners to adopt flexible, technology-friendly standards.

 - Distill legislative shifts into actionable business intelligence for executive leadership and ensure that our products and processes comply with evolving standards.

 - Identify and partner with trade associations, NGOs, and industry peers to amplify our legislative voice.



What You’ll Bring

 - Significant experience in energy regulatory affairs, with a heavy emphasis on the Illinois market; experience in government affairs is a plus.

 - Proven success negotiating with the ICC and strong familiarity with utilities, RTOs, and the General Assembly in Illinois.

 - Ability to interpret utility tariffs, load profiles, and technical grid requirements, then translate them for non-technical policymakers.

 - Understanding of how FERC rulings impact Illinois-specific energy programs.

 - A strong presence and exceptional public-speaking skills.

 - Ability to run independently to further a surging business.

 - Comfort with challenging the status quo and preconceived notions of what is possible.

 - Excellent communication skills, with the ability to distill complex concepts into clear, actionable advice.

 - An entrepreneurial mindset that thrives in ambiguity, moves fast, and prioritizes impact.

 - Passion for our work and a commitment to fueling American innovation, security, and prosperity through a more reliable grid for all.



Please note: Base is a startup, which means priorities shift and evolve quickly. Your role may expand or change based on the needs of the business at any given time, so the responsibilities listed may not be exhaustive.




OUR VALUES

 - First Principles Thinking: Question assumptions. Principles > rules.

 - Operate at Base Pace: Focus on what matters, act quickly, and learn by doing.

 - Give & Get Feedback: Be direct, be humble, and maintain a growth mindset.

 - Everyone’s an Owner: Follow through on commitments and own results.

 - Strong Opinions, Loosely Held: Drive clarity and make calls with imperfect information.

 - Committed to the Mission: Rebuilding the grid is a big challenge. We work hard because we care deeply about the impact we’re creating. We work in-person. It’s not a 9-to-5. We are all-in.

 - Fun & Optimism Coexist with Grit: Collaboration and celebration coincide with the intensity of building real things.
   
   


DO THE BEST WORK OF YOUR LIFE AT BASE.

Cox Fleet is currently hiring a  Mobile Diesel Technician Level II.
The Mobile Diesel Technician Level II  will be responsible for performing licensed DOT inspections, Preventative Maintenance inspections, light and follow-up repairs, light mechanical/hydraulic/electrical and electronic diagnostics, and other duties as assigned.  The Mobile Diesel Technician II can perform more advanced diagnostics and repairs under the supervision of a Sr Mobile Diesel Technician or higher. The Diesel Technician II continues to learn additional advanced mechanical skills and diagnostic techniques.  A successful Diesel Technician II complies with all company policies and achieves high level performance metrics.

Perform scheduled preventative maintenance (“PM”), DOT Inspections and follow up repairs on light, medium and heavy-duty vehicles in a mobile/field environment.
Perform minor adjustment and repairs on various types of truck equipment including, but not limited to the following: Electrical/Brake/Cooling Systems, Starters/Alternators, Fan clutches, Engine electronics, Diesel steering systems, Engines (gas and diesel), Transmissions (manual and automatic), Clutches, Differentials, etc.
Diagnose, adjust, and repair various types of truck equipment including, but not limited to the following: Electrical/Brake/Cooling Systems, Starters/Alternators, Air conditioning systems, Fan clutches, Engine electronics, Diesel steering systems, Engines (gas and diesel), Transmissions (manual and automatic), Clutches, Differentials, etc.
Inspect, test, and listen to defective equipment to diagnose malfunctions, using test instruments such as handheld computers and pressure gauges.
Road test vehicles to diagnose malfunctions and to ensure that they are working properly.
Identify problems, determine accuracy and relevance of information, using sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives.
Independently manage parts inventory and equipment provided on company-issued service truck and perform periodic reconciliation.
Maintain and operate company-issued service vehicle, conduct safety checks, and pre-/post-trip inspections of vehicle.
Work with and listen effectively to clients and customers to assess their needs, providing information or assistance, resolving their problems, or satisfying their expectations.

Work with a high degree of independence and manage own daily schedule.
Maintain a high level of productivity and be able to work within or close to most Standard Repair Times.

A critical role on the Cox Automotive Pricing Strategy team, the Senior Pricing Strategy Manager will lead cross-functional pricing, packaging and monetization initiatives for a specific Business Unit or Solution Set. This role is responsible for owning pricing initiatives from initial business question through strategy development, testing, recommendation and presentation to senior leadership.
This individual will operate as a strategic business consultant and trusted advisor, partnering across Product, Finance, Analytics, Marketing, Sales and business leadership to develop pricing recommendations that balance customer value, market dynamics, product performance and business objectives. Successful candidates will be comfortable working in situations where the answer is not immediately clear, determining what information or testing is needed and using sound business judgment to move an initiative forward.

Lead pricing initiatives from beginning to end, including defining the business question, developing the project approach, identifying required inputs, coordinating cross-functional partners, evaluating findings, developing recommendations and presenting conclusions to leadership.

Translate business, customer, product, financial and market insights into clear, actionable pricing recommendations.

Prior experience in consulting, professional services, or technology services sales.
Experience supporting ERP or cloud ERP transformation initiatives for mid-market organizations.

Demonstrated success developing partner relationships, generating qualified sales opportunities, and supporting revenue growth.

title: Director; Sales, Inventory & Operations Planning (SIOP) (Remote)
location: Remote - USA
description:
About MISUMI Americas
MISUMI Americas, a division of MISUMI Group, is a leading provider of standard, configurable, and custom manufacturing solutions. By integrating a vast catalog of components with a world-class digital manufacturing platform, MISUMI Americas empowers engineers and procurement teams to accelerate innovation across the entire product lifecycle. With operations in the San Francisco Bay Area and Chicago, the company serves as a vital partner for the most innovative companies in the Americas.
MISUMI Americas serves customers through regional sourcing teams and a network of QCTs (warehouses) that hold inventory close to demand. As the business grows, we need one clear, trusted process that connects what sales expects to sell with what we source, build and stock. This role creates and owns that process.
The Director, SIOP is the practice lead for Sales, Inventory & Operations Planning. Each month, they bring together a top-down view (business plan, targets, market signals) and a bottom-up view (account and regional forecasts) over a rolling horizon of six months or more. They turn that consensus demand into requirements by region and into the inventory each QCT must hold. Where supply cannot meet demand, they make the gap visible, size the impact on customer service and revenue, and consolidate the proposed fixes into clear investment options for the executive team.
The Director, SIOP is a peer of the Directors, Portfolio Management and works with them as partners. Portfolio Management owns what we offer: assortment, pricing, launches, exits and supplier capability. SIOP owns how much, where and when: consensus demand, regional supply requirements, QCT inventory targets and the monthly planning process. Phase 1 covers standard and configurable products and QCT inventory; custom process lines are covered through demand and partner-capacity visibility.
This is a Director role with a player-coach start: the person runs the process hands-on at first, then builds a small, highly capable team of planners and analysts. Success is measured by forecast accuracy, capacity utilization and, as the practice matures, inventory turns.
Own the monthly SIOP cycle: Design, run and keep improving the monthly process end to end: data refresh, demand review, supply review, reconciliation and the executive SIOP meeting. Set the calendar, the inputs each team owes and the decisions each step must produce.
Own the consensus demand number: Combine the business plan and targets with account and regional forecasts from Sales and the category overlay from each Portfolio Manager (launches, price changes, exits, competitive moves). Reconcile the views, explain the gaps and agree one demand plan over a rolling horizon of six months or more. Sales owns the account forecast; Portfolio Managers own the assumptions in their overlay; SIOP owns the process and the final number.
Translate demand into regional requirements: Map the consensus forecast to supply requirements by region, so regional sourcing teams know what volume and mix they must secure, and when.
Set inventory policy and QCT targets: Define safety stock, reorder logic and stocking depth by QCT and SKU class, to meet the service levels agreed in the executive SIOP review within the working-capital envelope set by Finance. Portfolio Managers decide which items are in the stocked set; SIOP decides how deep and where. Plan the run-down of items Portfolio Management decides to exit.
Run the input scorecard: Track whether Sales, Portfolio Management and Sourcing deliver complete, on-time and credible inputs each month, and publish the scorecard. The VP, Portfolio Management is the executive sponsor, chairs the monthly review and escalates late or weak Portfolio Management inputs. Late or weak Sales inputs escalate to the executive leadership team through the scorecard. The SVP, Operations & Supply Chain co-sponsors the supply-side inputs (Sourcing and QCTs) and escalates those.
Find and size supply and demand mismatches: Identify where demand will exceed supply or capacity, or where we hold inventory that demand does not support. Quantify revenue at risk and service impact. The relevant Portfolio Manager proposes the fix for their category or process; SIOP consolidates the proposals into the executive pre-read.
Lead the executive SIOP review: Prepare a concise monthly pre-read and run the executive meeting. Frame the decisions needed (investment, allocation, stocking, capacity), record what was decided and follow up on actions to closure.
Own the planning metrics: Define, measure and report forecast accuracy, capacity utilization and, as the practice matures, inventory turns. Set targets with the executive team and drive improvement over time.
Build the tools and data foundation: Work with Finance, Business Systems and Data teams to establish the planning data model, forecast history and dashboards the process needs. Choose and implement planning tools as the practice scales.
Build the team: Hire, develop and lead a small, high-performing team of demand and supply planners or analysts as the practice grows.
All employees are expected to maintain and contribute to the QMS.
Required
Experience: 10+ years in demand planning, supply planning, S&OP / IBP or supply chain operations, with at least 3–5 years leading the S&OP or SIOP process for a multi-region business.
Built a process before: A track record of designing and launching a monthly S&OP / SIOP cycle (not only taking part in one), and making it stick across sales, operations and finance.
Strong analytical skills: Fluent in forecasting methods, inventory policy (safety stock, service levels, reorder points) and capacity planning. Advanced Excel / Google Sheets; comfortable with BI tools and large data sets.
Influence without authority: Proven ability to hold sales and operations leaders accountable for inputs and commitments they do not report to you for.
Works as a peer of category owners: Gets the commercial story from category owners and stays out of assortment and pricing decisions.
Executive communication: Can turn complex planning data into a short, clear story with options and trade-offs for senior leaders.
Business judgment: Can build an investment case that links inventory and capacity decisions to service levels, revenue and working capital.
Leadership: Experience hiring and developing planners or analysts, or a strong readiness to build a team from scratch.
Education: Bachelor's degree in supply chain, operations, engineering, business or a related field.
Preferred
Industry: Experience in industrial distribution, manufacturing, configurable components or a high-SKU, make-to-order and stock business.
Network inventory: Experience setting inventory policy across a network of warehouses or distribution centers.
Planning tools: Hands-on experience with planning platforms (for example, Kinaxis, o9, Anaplan, SAP IBP or similar) and ERP data.
Global and matrixed work: Experience in a multinational company, including work with a parent company or stakeholders across cultures and time zones.
Certification: APICS / ASCM (CPIM or CSCP) or similar is a plus; an MBA or advanced degree is a plus.
AI and automation: Interest in using AI and automation to improve forecasting and reduce manual planning work.
Primarily remote, computer-based work, including extended periods at a computer and on video calls. Occasional visits to QCT (warehouse) and supplier sites, which involve walking, standing and following site safety rules.
Ability to travel up to 20% annually, mainly within the Americas, for QCT and regional sourcing visits, team meetings and offsites, with occasional international travel to work with MISUMI Group planning teams.
Benefits include, but are not limited to:
Comprehensive medical and dental coverage
401(k) plan
Generous PTO and leave programs
Salary Range:  $194,360 - $245,220 per year; based upon experience

Bring diverse perspectives and experience to our culture and company.
Excel at being part of a strong, empathetic team.
Thrive in an environment emphasizing respect, honesty, collaboration, and growth.
Have an ‘always learning’ mindset that celebrates learning, not just wins.
Help us continue to build a world-class organization that values the contributions of all of our teammates

 - Experience commissioning furnaces or other thermal equipment, working with vendors through FAT, SAT, startup, and qualification.

 - Structured, data-driven troubleshooting of thermal, atmosphere, instrumentation, and equipment issues, with working knowledge of thermocouples, PID control, and root cause analysis.

description:

Formic is on a mission to reshape American manufacturing by making automation accessible to every factory. As labor constraints rise, costs increase, and global competition intensifies, automation is no longer optional for manufacturers that want to stay competitive.

Backed by leading investors including Lux Capital, Initialized Capital, Blackhorn Ventures, and Mitsubishi HC Capital North America, Formic is scaling rapidly and building the foundation for a new era of high-performance, Made in America production.
About the Role
We're looking for an AI-native, technically resourceful operator to rethink how IT works at Formic. You'll own the day-to-day technology experience for Formicans, from devices, applications, and employee support to infrastructure, security fundamentals, and external technology partners. This is a hands-on individual contributor role with significant autonomy: you'll solve immediate problems while building smarter, more reliable systems that prevent them from recurring.
If the Wi-Fi is down, someone's account isn't working, a conference room isn't connecting, a new hire needs a laptop, or a critical application goes offline, you're the person who makes sure it gets handled. You aren't expected to personally pull every cable, configure every system, or solve every specialized security issue. You are expected to own the outcome.
You don't need to know every system we use on Day 1. We'd rather hire someone with strong technical fundamentals, exceptional resourcefulness, and an ability to learn quickly. Over time, we expect you to become an expert in Formic's technology environment and help shape how our systems evolve as we grow.
You do need to be highly capable at using AI to extend what you can do. We want someone who is genuinely excited about technology and constantly asks: Why are we doing this manually? Can I automate it? Can I make this better?
AI and automation are central to this job, not side projects. We want someone who connects AI to real systems and workflows, builds practical automations, experiments responsibly, and measures whether their work makes Formic faster and more effective.
The goal is simple: technology becomes something the company rarely has to think about because it simply works.
In this role, you will:
Own Employee IT
Serve as the internal owner of day-to-day IT support, troubleshooting issues across Mac and Windows devices, applications, accounts, authentication, peripherals, and connectivity.
Own the technology experience throughout the employee lifecycle, including onboarding, offboarding, equipment provisioning and recovery, account configuration, permissions, and secure access removal.
Administer our device fleet, including MDM/RMM, patching, encryption, endpoint protection, software deployment, remote management, and remote lock/wipe capabilities.
Maintain an accurate hardware inventory and manage the full equipment lifecycle, including purchasing, configuration, deployment, repairs, replacements, shipping, and returns.
Administer systems such as Google Workspace, Slack, Notion, 1Password, Microsoft 365, Apple Business Manager, VPN, and other SaaS applications.
Manage identities, accounts, groups, permissions, licenses, MFA, SSO, and application access.
Maintain clear, accurate, and accessible documentation of our systems, configurations, processes, and administrative access.
Establish effective IT support processes for request intake, prioritization, escalation, resolution tracking, and employee communication.
Identify recurring issues, address root causes, and implement solutions that reduce support requests and improve the employee technology experience.
Own IT Infrastructure & Office Technology
Own the reliability and functionality of our internet, Wi-Fi, networking, conference rooms, displays, AV equipment, printers, shared devices, and other onsite technology.
Manage and troubleshoot network infrastructure, including routers, switches, firewalls, wireless access points, VPNs, and connectivity issues.
Own the technology supporting physical security, including badge access systems and security cameras, partnering with internal teams and external specialists as needed.
Ensure conference rooms and shared technology are consistently reliable, functional, and ready for use.
Resolve onsite technology issues and coordinate with ISPs, network engineers, low-voltage contractors, security vendors, and other technical specialists when needed.
Drive technology installations, infrastructure upgrades, office expansions, and other IT-related projects.
Maintain organized and readily available IT equipment, spare devices, networking hardware, and accessories.
Proactively monitor infrastructure, anticipate potential issues, and implement improvements that minimize downtime and strengthen system reliability.
Automate Relentlessly
Use AI as a force multiplier in your own work, actively experimenting with emerging tools and technologies.
Identify repetitive, inefficient, or manual processes across IT operations and the broader Formic organization that can be eliminated, simplified, or automated.
Design, build, and maintain workflows using AI agents, APIs, scripts, integrations, and automation platforms.
Automate provisioning, onboarding, offboarding, technical support, inventory management, documentation, reporting, and other recurring IT processes wherever practical.
Build lightweight internal tools when developing a solution makes more sense than purchasing another piece of software.
Leverage AI to improve troubleshooting, system monitoring, knowledge management, and employee self-service.
Help Formic evaluate and adopt technologies that make our teams faster, smarter, and more effective.
Measure the effectiveness of automations and continuously improve our systems and processes with scalability, reliability, and security in mind.
Own IT Security Fundamentals & External Partners
Serve as Formic's internal owner of our managed IT and security provider relationships, maintaining accountability for systems, services, and outcomes.
Partner with external specialists on endpoint security, EDR/MDR, networking, vulnerability management, monitoring, and incident response.
Establish and maintain effective baseline security controls, including MFA, encryption, patching, endpoint protection, device management, and access controls.
Support SOC 2 and other compliance initiatives through accurate documentation, control implementation, system inventories, and evidence collection.
Maintain visibility into device compliance, vulnerabilities, access controls, and administrative privileges, ensuring identified risks are tracked through remediation.
Exercise sound technical judgment in determining what to resolve internally and when to engage external specialists.
Hold vendors accountable for responsiveness, service quality, timelines, costs, and outcomes.
Continuously evaluate the effectiveness of our external IT partnerships, identifying opportunities to improve service delivery, operational efficiency, and cost effectiveness.
Assess which IT capabilities should be developed internally versus supported by
Bonus Points if you have:
Worked in a startup or physical operating environment.
Administered Google Workspace, MDM/RMM, EDR, or identity systems.
Supported SOC 2 or other security compliance frameworks.
Worked effectively with external IT providers and held partners accountable for service quality and outcomes.
Worked with office networking, firewalls, VPNs, or physical-security systems.
Experience implementing or improving IT ticketing, asset management, monitoring, or employee self-service systems.
Built scripts, bots, internal tools, integrations, or AI agents because you got tired of doing something manually.
Created a home lab, side project, GitHub repo, Raspberry Pi graveyard, overly complicated Home Assistant setup, or other evidence that you genuinely enjoy messing with technology also counts.

If this sounds like you, Formic may be the right place for you!

Your automation and quality gates directly safeguard multi-billion-transistor TPU schedules, catching cross-view discrepancies before they reach physical implementation and signoff. Because you will partner with Physical Design, Static Timing Analysis (STA), CAD Methodology, and foundry partners, this role offers an end-to-end view of advanced-node chip execution—with direct mentorship and room to grow your ownership across Google's silicon infrastructure.

The Director, Global Credit and Reporting provides global leadership for commercial credit strategy, credit risk management, and accounts receivable reporting. Monitor global customer credit exposure, concentration risk, payment performance, aging trends, and changing economic or market conditions; drive timely mitigation actions.

Own global accounts receivable reporting and executive dashboards, ensuring consistent definitions, data quality, controls, and timely distribution across regions and business units.

Establish performance targets and governance routines for aging, DSO, bad debt, collections, disputes, and other global AR KPIs; coordinate corrective action plans where performance is outside expectations.
Partner with Accounts Receivable leadership to prioritize past-due portfolios, accelerate cash conversion, resolve payment barriers, and minimize bad debt and write-off risk.

Lead global standardization and continuous improvement across credit and AR reporting processes, including systems, master data, controls, workflow, and management reporting.
Sponsor technology and automation initiatives, including business requirements, user acceptance testing, implementation, adoption, and post-launch performance monitoring.
Maintain effective internal controls and documentation, including support for SOX, internal audit, external audit, and policy compliance requirements.
Build trusted relationships with senior stakeholders and communicate complex credit and AR matters clearly, including risks, trade-offs, decisions, and recommended actions.
Required Skills and Experience
12 or more years of progressive experience in commercial credit, accounts receivable, collections, order-to-cash, finance, or a related discipline, including significant leadership responsibility in a complex global organization.
Demonstrated experience leading global credit risk programs and managing large, complex business-to-business receivables portfolios.
Advanced financial statement analysis and credit underwriting skills, including assessment of liquidity, leverage, cash flow, industry risk, and customer solvency.
Strong command of global AR reporting and performance management, including aging, DSO, delinquency, collection effectiveness, bad debt, write-offs, reserves, disputes, and unapplied cash.
Proven ability to design executive dashboards, establish KPI definitions, analyze trends and variances, and convert data into practical actions.
Experience establishing policies, controls, approval matrices, governance, and escalation frameworks across multiple countries or regions.
Demonstrated success leading process transformation, systems implementation, automation, and data-quality improvement.
Strong stakeholder management and executive communication skills.
Ability to make sound independent decisions, manage competing priorities, and operate effectively in a dynamic, matrixed environment.
Required Education and Training
Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, Economics, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience.
Working Conditions
General office and remote-work conditions. Ability to work across global time zones as business needs require. International and domestic travel may be required, up to 20%.
Preferred Skills and Experience
Master’s degree in Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, or a related field.
Professional certification such as CPA, CMA, CFA, CCE, or equivalent credit or finance credential.
Experience with SAP or another global enterprise resource planning system, credit-risk platforms, business intelligence and AI tools, and advanced Excel.
Experience with shared-services or globally distributed operating models and multi-currency receivables.
Knowledge of US GAAP considerations related to credit losses, bad debt, and allowance methodologies.
Experience supporting acquisitions, integrations, and global process harmonization.

As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
W hat We Are Looking For
The Future Forward AI Research group within Intuitive Surgical has an immediate opening in Sunnyvale, CA for a Machine Learning Engineer with focus on surgical image/ video analysis, and multi-modal foundation models, contributing to new technology development for next-generation robot-assisted surgery platforms. This role is an exciting opportunity to join a newly formed team and contribute to its growth and it will give you an opportunity to test your knowledge in a challenging problem-solving environment.
The successful candidate must excel in a high-energy, focused, small-team environment, be able to contribute to advanced product development, and have a commitment to high research quality. A strong sense of shared responsibility and shared reward is required.
Key Responsibilities
Contribute to research, design, and implementation of AI algorithms for computer vision (image and video analysis), multi-modal data and generative systems.
Contribute to development of effective techniques and infrastructure, from the initial idea to the running prototype and product.
Contribute to research projects that develop a variety of algorithms and systems in computer vision, robotics, and multi-modal data fusion.
Advance the state-of-the-art in the field, including generating patents and publications.
Develop validation methods and evaluation metrics to show scalability to large clinical datasets.
Contribute to building new clinical datasets and data pipelines.
Participate in integration of new ML/CV algorithms into existing and future robotic platforms.
Experiment with several users and clinical advisors to iterate prototype designs based on feedback and performance.
Develop new technologies and digital products to improve surgeon and team performance on robotic surgery platforms.
Support academic collaborations in related fields.
Experience and Abilities
Doctoral degree in computer science, electrical and computer engineering, or Master's degree with minimum (5) years industry experience developing computer vision and machine learning applications.
Strong understanding and experience in building effective learning systems (data collection, training, evaluation, and making iterative improvements).
Strong publication track record in conferences like CVPR, ICCV, MICCAI, etc.
Strong hands-on experience with at least one of the mainstream deep learning frameworks such as TensorFlow or PyTorch.
Strong hands-on experience with Python (proficiency), C/C++ (proficiency), Shell Script
Strong engineering practices, debugging/profiling skills, familiarity with multi-threaded programming.
Strong  hands-on experience with GPU accelerated algorithms and implementations.
Strong  hands-on experience with state-of-the-art AI models.
Excellent communication skills both written and verbal.
Interested in early phases of product exploration and iteration based on incomplete requirements.
Solid understanding of computer vision, machine learning, and deep learning algorithms and techniques is required.
Experience with visualization tools is a plus.
Self-starter and able to work in a collaborative and results-oriented environment.
Ability to travel domestically and internationally (5-15%)
Able to view live and recorded surgical procedures.

Primary Function of Position
We are seeking a Platform & Solutions Architect - ServiceNow to own the technical architecture of our enterprise- ServiceNow platform. This role will sets platform-level design direction, translates business requirements into scalable, secure, and highly performant ServiceNow solutions, and maintains consistency across modules, workflows, integrations, and geographies.
The architect serves as the ServiceNow technical design authority within established enterprise architecture, information security, and platform governance.  The role will partner with enterprise architects, business stakeholders, and technical teams to define future-state roadmaps, design end-to-end solutions, and establish best practices and governance across the organization. They will serve as a thought leader for ServiceNow architecture, enabling digital transformation while ensuring platform consistency, compliance, and scalability.
Essential Job Duties
Platform Architecture & Strategic Planning
Owns and maintains ServiceNow target-state reference architecture and prioritized technical roadmap spanning ITSM, ITOM, HRSD, SPM and other modules and scoped applications.
Evaluate emerging technologies and industry trends; translate into organizational strategies, architecture principles, and actionable design patterns.
Advise senior leaders and stakeholders on platform capabilities, architectural trade-offs, technical risk, sustainability, best practices, alignment with security, data, identity, and enterprise technology strategies.
Solution Architecture & Delivery
Lead architecture and design of complex ServiceNow solutions, including scoped applications, workflows, automation, and integrations.
Drive architecture across multiple domains and ensure alignment with enterprise goals, security, compliance, and governance.
Lead proofs-of-concept, pilot programs, and feasibility studies for innovative platform capabilities.
Ensure robust platform performance, maintainability, and scalability across environments.
Review and challenge implementation partner and vendor designs; ensure key architectural decisions are documented, and appropriate internal technical ownership is retained.
Integration & Data Architecture
Design enterprise integrations with systems such as Workday, ERP, HRIS, cloud platforms, and other enterprise applications using REST/SOAP APIs, MID Server, ETL, and iPaaS solutions.
Establish secure integration and access patterns for service accounts, external tools, and automated agents, applying least privilege, traceability, and appropriate approval controls.
Define data architecture, CMDB models, and service mapping strategies to support enterprise operational needs.
Architecture Governance, Policy, & Decision Rights
Establish and enforce architectural standards, reference models, and development guidelines.
Review, approve, and guide solution designs to ensure compliance with enterprise policies and security requirements.
Develop, publish, and maintain architectural artifacts, blueprints, and technical documentation for enterprise consumption.
Leadership & Collaboration
Provide mentorship and technical guidance to development teams, architects, and IT leaders.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams, business owners, and product managers to ensure solution adoption and alignment.
Influence enterprise decisions and foster a culture of innovation, architectural excellence, and best practices.
Continuous Improvement
Stay current on ServiceNow releases, capabilities, and industry best practices.
Identify opportunities to optimize, automate, and innovate ServiceNow processes using AI, automation, and emerging platform features.
Required Skills and Experience
15+ years of IT experience, with 7+ years in ServiceNow architecture or development.
Deep expertise across multiple ServiceNow suites (ITSM, ITOM, HRSD, SPM) and scoped/custom applications.
Proven experience in enterprise architecture, platform governance, and solution design.
Expertise in ServiceNow integrations, including REST/SOAP APIs, MID Server, ETL, and iPaaS platforms.
Strong knowledge of CMDB, Discovery, Service Mapping, security, and platform performance best practices.
Excellent stakeholder management, communication, and influence skills at Director/VP levels.
ServiceNow certifications: CSA, CAD required; CIS, CTA, or CMA highly preferred.
Experience in leading global, multi-domain ServiceNow initiatives.
Experience with AI/automation capabilities within ServiceNow (GenAI, Predictive Intelligence, Now Assist).
Ability to drive business value through architectural thought leadership and platform innovation.
Required Education and Training
Bachelor’s degree required, Master’s preferred.
Preferred Skills and Experience
ServiceNow Certified System Administrator (CSA).
ServiceNow Certified Application Developer (CAD).
Relevant ServiceNow AI or Now Assist certifications.

title: Senior Biostatistician
location: Sunnyvale, CA, US
description:
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of Position
As a key member of the Clinical Affairs department, the Senior Biostatistician (Biostatistician IV)
provides advanced statistical expertise to support the design, conduct, and analysis of clinical
studies, ranging from early pre-market to post-market evidence generation. The Biostatistician
IV is the statistical subject matter expert working in cross-functional teams, managing
roadmaps and priorities to ensure timely and high quality delivery of results. This role serves as
a nearly independent statistical lead, providing technical leadership by improving analysis
processes, mentoring junior staff, and managing a diverse project portfolio to ensure that
clinical evidence meets the highest standards for regulatory submissions and scientific
publication.
Roles & Responsibilities
• Study Design & Protocol Development: Lead the writing of statistical sections for
complex clinical protocols with limited supervision, ensuring robust study designs,
hypothesis tests, power analyses, and sample size justifications.
• Data Analysis: Utilize appropriate and robust statistical and programming methodology
in the analysis of clinical trial data, including complex and advanced methods as needed,
ensuring high-quality results for regulatory submissions and scientific publications.
• Clinical Operations Roadmap: Serve as the Biostatistics representative in core team
meetings, setting functional roadmaps and managing stakeholder expectations.
• Portfolio Management: Manage a portfolio of 3–7 projects simultaneously and take
ownership of one specific business or functional area.
• Team Communication: Interpret complex statistical results for cross-functional teams in
a clear and actionable manner, considering clinical implications and proactively offering
alternative solutions.
• Scientific Literature and Evidence Generation: Independently search and learn from
scientific literature. Write complete methods, results, and analysis interpretation
sections with supervision for regulatory submissions, compliance, scientific journals, and
medical conferences. Explore novel biostatistical & programming methodology
applications.
• External Engagement: Engage with external stakeholders, including regulatory agencies,
Principal Investigators (PIs), and Key Opinion Leaders (KOLs) to define requirements,
generate deliverables, and gather feedback.
• Data Management Support: Partner with Data Management to co-standardize edit
specifications, critical variable lists, data structures, and extraction workflows to ensure
data integrity and scalability.
• Process Improvement: Improve standardization and quality control of analysis pipelines
across projects, ensuring high-quality results for regulatory submissions and scientific
publications. Improve and implement SOPs and WIs for Statistical Analysis Plans (SAPs)
and mock Tables, Listings, and Figures (TLFs), balancing flexibility and consistency across
studies.
• Mentorship: Provide guidance and leadership to junior biostatisticians.
• Regulatory Compliance: Ensure all activities strictly adhere to Good Clinical Practice
(GCP), ISO 14155, and 21 CFR Part 812 regulations
Skills, Experience, Education, & Training
• Minimum Degree: Master’s (MS) or Ph.D. in Biostatistics or Statistics.
• Professional Experience: Minimum of 6 years of experience with an MS, or 3 years with
a Ph.D..
• Industry Experience: Minimum of 4 years of experience in clinical trials, surgical medical
device clinical research strongly preferred.
• Statistical Methods: Proven expertise in advanced and complex statistical
methodologies, including experience with adaptive designs or Bayesian methods.
• Programming: Mastery of R preferred, SAS and Python also considered; ability to write
clean, functional, modular code for a team development environment and train junior
team members in best practices.
• Independence & Leadership: Demonstrated ability to work nearly independently while
providing functional mentorship to junior biostatisticians.
• External Reputation: Track record of strong professional relationships within the
external scientific (biostatistics, medical devices, clinical trials) and/or regulatory
community.
• Communication: Excellent verbal and written communication, teamwork, and
interpersonal skills with both technical and non-technical constituents.
Logistics
• Location: Preference will be given to candidates able to be onsite in Sunnyvale,
California or willing to relocate.
• Travel: Position may require up to 10% travel.

location: Home Office (CA) - Los Angeles
description:
Invenergy is North America’s largest privately held developer, owner, and operator of power infrastructure. With 25 years of trusted execution, we deliver reliable, affordable energy through a diverse portfolio that includes natural gas, solar, land-based wind, energy storage, transmission, and domestic manufacturing. Headquartered in Chicago, we develop, own, and operate large scale projects that power communities and support the energy future.
This position will be open for application for at least 3 calendar days from the posting date. This position will remain open for application based on business need, which may be before or after the 3-day posting window.
Job Description
Cybersecurity Architect
Position Overview
The Cybersecurity Architect provides enterprise-level technical and architectural leadership to advance the organization’s cybersecurity strategy and long-term technology direction. This role translates business and technology strategy into comprehensive, executable cybersecurity architecture and roadmaps that address current and emerging risks while supporting the organization’s broader enterprise technology objectives.
Operating across infrastructure, applications, networks, cloud, operational technology, data, and security platforms, the Cybersecurity Architect works closely with senior technology leaders and other architectural disciplines to establish enterprise standards, evaluate emerging technologies, and guide technology decisions with an 18–36 month outlook.
The role serves as a senior technical leader and individual contributor, focusing on architectural direction and influence rather than formal personnel management. The Cybersecurity Architect also develops organizational capability through technical mentorship, knowledge sharing, training, and the introduction and advancement of new cybersecurity concepts and practices.
Responsibilities
Enterprise Cybersecurity Architecture & Strategy
Translate organizational and technology strategy into comprehensive cybersecurity architectures, standards, and executable technology roadmaps.
Develop and maintain an 18–36 month cybersecurity architecture roadmap aligned with enterprise technology direction, business priorities, and evolving risk.
Serve as a key contributor to enterprise-level technology strategy and architecture discussions with senior technology leadership.
Define and advance enterprise cybersecurity architecture across applications, infrastructure, networks, cloud, operational technology, data, identity, and security platforms.
Establish architectural principles, patterns, reference architectures, and technical standards that provide consistency and long-term stability across the enterprise.
Evaluate emerging cybersecurity technologies, architectural approaches, and industry developments and determine their applicability to the organization.
Translate new or emerging technical concepts into practical architectural standards and solutions that can be adopted across business and technology domains.
Partner with application, infrastructure, network, cloud, data, and other technology architects to develop secure, resilient, scalable, and cost-effective enterprise solutions.
Architecture Governance & Risk
Provide architectural review and guidance for significant technology initiatives to ensure alignment with enterprise cybersecurity standards and strategy.
Review and approve security architecture and security design for applications, platforms, infrastructure, and enterprise technology solutions.
Identify current and emerging cybersecurity risks and translate those risks into architectural requirements and longer-term technology strategies.
Establish security architecture patterns for common enterprise use cases, including corporate offices, generation facilities, cloud environments, applications, and operational technology.
Guide the architectural use and integration of security technologies including identity and access management, firewalls, VPNs, network security, endpoint security, intrusion detection and prevention, and other cybersecurity platforms.
Develop architectural solutions that appropriately balance cybersecurity, operational, business, financial, and technology requirements.
Ensure cybersecurity architecture supports applicable regulatory requirements, industry standards, and organizational policies.
Provide architectural guidance for significant cybersecurity events or operational issues when they have material enterprise-level impact.
Enterprise Technology Leadership & Influence
Serve as a senior technical authority for cybersecurity architecture and enterprise security technology decisions.
Influence enterprise technology decisions across multiple platforms and technical domains without relying on direct organizational authority.
Work closely with senior technology leadership to evaluate strategic technology investments, architectural direction, technology lifecycle decisions, and enterprise cybersecurity priorities.
Provide deep technical and architectural guidance to engineering, operations, application, infrastructure, security, and business teams.
Introduce, formalize, and advance new cybersecurity concepts, technologies, and architectural practices across the organization.
Mentor and develop technical staff through architectural guidance, knowledge sharing, training, and technical leadership.
Communicate complex cybersecurity concepts and architectural decisions effectively to both technical and non-technical audiences.
Promote continuous improvement of enterprise cybersecurity architecture, standards, engineering practices, and technical capabilities.
Technology Innovation & External Engagement
Maintain awareness of evolving cybersecurity threats, technologies, architecture practices, and industry trends and assess their potential enterprise impact.
Conduct strategic evaluations and proof-of-concept activities for emerging technologies and cybersecurity capabilities.
Build productive relationships with technology vendors and strategic partners to evaluate, enhance, and, where appropriate, develop solutions that address enterprise requirements.
Participate in relevant industry organizations, professional communities, conferences, working groups, or other forums to maintain current knowledge and contribute to the advancement of cybersecurity practices.
Represent the organization in technical discussions with customers, vendors, partners, and other external stakeholders when appropriate.
Minimum Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent industry or military experience.
10+ years of progressive experience across cybersecurity, technology architecture, engineering, infrastructure, or related enterprise technology disciplines.
Demonstrated experience developing enterprise cybersecurity architectures and translating technology strategy into executable roadmaps.
Demonstrated experience working across multiple technology domains such as applications, infrastructure, cloud, networks, databases, operational technology, identity, and cybersecurity platforms.
Experience influencing significant technology decisions and establishing technical standards across multiple teams or business areas.
Demonstrated ability to move between strategic architecture discussions and the technical detail necessary to translate concepts into executable solutions.
Experience working effectively with senior technology leaders, architects, engineers, business stakeholders, vendors, and strategic partners.
Eligible to work in the United States without the need for employer visa sponsorship now or in the future.
Preferred Qualifications
Master’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent combination of advanced education and significant industry or military experience.
Professional certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CISA, SABSA, TOGAF, or comparable cybersecurity or enterprise architecture credentials.
Experience developing security architecture for Operational Technology (OT), industrial control systems, or critical infrastructure environments.
Demonstrated participation or leadership in cybersecurity or technology professional organizations.
Experience presenting, publishing, teaching, or otherwise contributing technical expertise to professional or industry communities.
Experience partnering with technology vendors to evaluate, modify, or develop solutions for complex enterprise requirements.

$180,000.00 - $225,000.00 USD Annual
Bonus: 30% - 40%

Job Description:
Changing the World, One Kibble at a Time
Champion Petfoods is expanding! We are excited to announce we are looking for an Breakthrough Innovation Manager to join our rapidly growing company.
Champion Petfoods is an award-winning pet food crafter with a reputation of trust spanning 35+ years. From our humble beginnings, founded in a small town in Alberta, Canada, Champion – with its ORIJEN® and ACANA® brands – is a key player in the global premium pet food industry. Our purpose,  To Earn Pet Lover Trust Every Day so Pets Thrive for a Lifetime ,  provides the foundation for our highest aspirations as a company.
Being a partner to the communities that surround us – and the environment that sustains us – are top priorities.
We would love to hear from you if you are passionate about personal and professional growth and see yourself as a key player contributing to our continued success as an award-winning company.
Here’s the scoop - Summary
Champion Petfoods is looking for a curious, creative and highly collaborative marketer to help shape the future of pet nutrition.
The Global Marketing Breakthrough Innovation Manager will identify emerging needs and new-to-category opportunities by connecting consumer insights, scientific discovery, market signals and ideas from across the Mars ecosystem.
This role focuses on the earliest stages of innovation: finding promising spaces, developing concepts and validating them with consumers and cross-functional partners.
Once an opportunity is sufficiently defined and validated, the role will prepare a clear handoff to the Global Innovation Managers, who will lead development and commercialization.
The Breakthrough Innovation Manager works out of our Corporate office in either Edmonton, AB or Louisville, CO on a hybrid schedule with 3 days in-person.
What a typical day looks like
Scan for emerging consumer needs, technologies, ingredients, behaviors and category shifts across pet care, human food and adjacent sectors.
Build relationships across the Mars ecosystem to exchange ideas, find relevant expertise and uncover potential innovation opportunities.
Partner closely with the R&I Discovery team to explore scientific advances, capabilities and early-stage solutions that could address future pet and pet parent needs.
Work with Consumer and Market Insights (CMI) to turn consumer, market and cultural insights into opportunity areas and distinctive concepts.
Create and refine breakthrough concepts, including the consumer problem, target audience, core proposition, potential benefit and reasons to believe.
Design and coordinate learning plans to test assumptions and validate concepts with consumers and internal partners.
Connect insights from different sources to identify patterns, challenge conventional thinking and reveal opportunities that may not be obvious within the pet food category alone.
Assess the strategic fit, potential relevance and early feasibility of opportunities with partners across Brand, R&I, Supply, Regulatory and other functions.
Maintain a forward-looking pipeline of opportunity areas, concepts, evidence and key learning.
Prepare concise recommendations for leadership and innovation governance forums.
Develop clear handoff briefs for Innovation Managers, including the opportunity, consumer evidence, concept direction, assumptions, risks and recommended next steps.
Stay connected with receiving Innovation Managers during handoff to support continuity of the concept and its supporting rationale.
What you'll bring
5+ years of experience in marketing, innovation, consumer insights, strategy, foresight or a related field. Ideally in breakthrough natural or human food industry.
Experience developing consumer-led ideas, concepts or new growth opportunities.
Strong creative thinking and the ability to explore possibilities beyond familiar category conventions.
A talent for connecting information across consumers, markets, science, technology and business needs.
Strong collaboration and networking skills, including the confidence to build relationships across teams and functions.
Comfort working with ambiguity and turning early, incomplete signals into clear questions and testable concepts.
Experience partnering with insights, R&I or other technical teams is an advantage.
Experience in consumer packaged goods, premium/natural food, pet care or another innovation-led industry is an advantage.
Clear communication and storytelling skills, including the ability to explain an opportunity and the evidence behind it.
Curiosity, adaptability and a willingness to learn through experimentation.
How success will be measured
A pipeline of well-framed, relevant breakthrough opportunities.
Quality of consumer and market evidence used to shape and validate concepts.
Strength of collaboration with CMI, R&I Discovery and Mars ecosystem partners.
Clear, actionable handoffs that enable Innovation Managers to advance promising opportunities.
Progress in developing concepts that address future pet and pet parent needs.
What can you expect from Champion?
Safety:  a strong commitment to ensure all people are provided with a safe, healthy and respectful environment.

US: USD $105,000-$140,000 annual salary, annual bonus eligibility, and 401k with company matching.
Canada: $87,000-$115,000 annual salary, annual bonus eligibility, and RRSP with company matching.
Industry Competitive Benefits:  Medical, dental, vision and employee assistance programs to meet your individual or family needs.
Continuing Education:  In house & online learning & development, as well as an education assistance program.
Quality:  a dedication to uphold the highest standards of authenticity, nutritional integrity, and food safety, to earn the trust of Pet Lovers everywhere.
Other Perks:  Free bag of premium pet food each month.

Mars Snacking is seeking a visionary, technically accomplished, and commercially minded Product Line Director, Omnichannel Experiences and D2C Commerce Technology. This leader will direct the strategy, architecture, lifecycle, and value realization of our global Direct-to-Consumer (D2C) and omnichannel commerce platforms.
Operating at the critical intersection of modern commerce technology, consumer experience, and commercial performance, this role serves as the technology anchor translating complex business ambitions into scalable, future-ready digital platforms. In close partnership with the Omnichannel Experiences & D2C Commercial Director and regional business units, you will champion Mars Snacking’s Digital Product Line operating model.
You will directly lead, mentor, and inspire a world-class team of Technology Product Owners (TPOs) and Technical/Business Analysts, driving product excellence, architectural integrity, and measurable business outcomes across global brands and retail channels.
What Are We Looking For?
Education: Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Software Engineering, Business Technology, or equivalent practical experience; an MBA or relevant business qualification is an asset.
Progressive Leadership: 10+ years of progressive technology leadership experience across digital commerce, enterprise architecture, and platform delivery, including 5+ years directly managing and mentoring high-performing teams of Technology Product Owners, Systems/Business Analysts, and cross-functional product squads.
Business Acumen & Strategic Value Creation: Exceptional business acumen with a demonstrated record of connecting technology investments directly to commercial outcomes (revenue growth, conversion rate optimization, margin expansion, customer lifetime value, and operational efficiencies). Adept at speaking the language of business leaders and brand teams.
Product Line & Operating Model Excellence: Proven success establishing and scaling Agile Product Line operating models, driving outcome-driven roadmaps, rigorous backlog prioritization, OKRs, discovery processes, and modern product management governance.
Modern Commerce Architecture: Deep technical comprehension of composable commerce architectures (MACH: Microservices, API-first, Cloud-native, Headless) and enterprise platforms (e.g., Salesforce Commerce Cloud, Shopify Plus, commerce tools, etc).
Enterprise Integration & Ecosystem Knowledge: Strong foundation in API ecosystems, event-driven architectures, middleware/iPaaS, ERP integrations (SAP), Product Information Management (PIM), Digital Asset Management (DAM), and Order Management Systems (OMS).
Omnichannel & Data/AI Mastery: Proven track record delivering unified commerce capabilities combined with modern Customer Data Platforms (CDP), identity resolution, personalization engines, and practical AI/ML applications in retail.
Vendor & Partner Governance: Extensive experience steering multi-vendor ecosystems, software vendors, system integrators (SIs), and digital agencies to ensure technical quality, accountability, and commercial value.
People Leadership & Coaching: Inspiring people leader skilled at coaching Product Owners and Analysts to bridge technical feasibility with business desirability and operational viability.
What Will Be Your Key Responsibilities?
Technology Product Team Leadership & Capability Building
Lead & Mentor TPOs and Analysts: Lead, coach, and develop a team of Technology Product Owners and Technical/Business Analysts, fostering deep domain expertise, technical curiosity, and commercial awareness.
Product Management Rigor: Establish standard methodologies for technical product discovery, backlog grooming, user story definition, functional requirements mapping, acceptance criteria, and value tracking across all squads.
Bridge Business & Technology: Guide your team in translating broad commercial visions and brand strategies into crisp, actionable technical specifications, feature roadmaps, and architectural runway.
Technology Strategy, Architecture & Composable Vision
Unified Commerce Tech Strategy: Define, own, and execute the multi-year technology vision and platform roadmap supporting Mars Snacking’s global D2C and omnichannel footprint.
Composable & Headless Transition: Champion MACH principles and headless architectures, balancing leading-edge innovation with pragmatic enterprise scalability, reusability, and total cost of ownership (TCO).
Platform Harmonization: Drive standardization and core platform harmonization across global brands, markets, and regional operating units while providing local teams the agility to meet market-specific consumer expectations.
Commercial Alignment & Omnichannel Value Delivery
Commercial Partnership: Partner hand-in-hand with the D2C & Omnichannel teams, brand marketing leaders, and retail operations to co-create roadmaps aligned to P&L growth and consumer engagement targets.
Seamless Omnichannel Journeys: Drive technical realization of unified commerce experiences spanning digital storefronts, retail flagship stores, mobile apps, social commerce, POS systems, and loyalty programs.
Fulfillment & Transactional Capabilities: Oversee end-to-end enablement of core commerce services including unified inventory visibility, distributed order routing, omni-fulfillment, omnichannel customer service, and international payment gateways.
Enterprise Integration, Data & AI Innovation
Enterprise Connectivity: Oversee the architectural harmony and integration integrity between commerce platforms and core enterprise backbones (SAP ERP, OMS, DAM,CRM etc).
Data-Driven Personalization & AI: Drive the roadmap for Customer Data Platforms (CDPs), identity unification, and real-time segmentation, leveraging predictive and generative AI to deliver personalized consumer touchpoints at scale.
Commerce Analytics & Observability: Partner with analytics teams to implement unified telemetry, observability, and reporting tools that measure system performance alongside business KPIs (funnel conversion, AOV, churn, and NPS).
Operational Excellence, Governance & Partner Orchestration
Reliability & Security: Maintain end-to-end accountability for platform uptime, peak-event readiness (e.g., Cyber Week, seasonal drops), security, data privacy (GDPR, CCPA), and compliance across all digital touchpoints.
Product Line Governance & Tech Debt: Steer product lifecycle governance, platform modernization programs, and technical debt remediation to ensure agility and sustainability.
Strategic Vendor Management: Direct relationships, contracts, and delivery quality with SaaS platform providers, systems integrators, and software engineering partners.
