title: Retail Sales Manager - Fort Wayne South, IN
location: USA-Indiana-Fort Wayne
description:
Job Description:
The Mars Retail Sales Manager is responsible for executing Mars Sales Strategy by applying fact-based selling techniques to influence customer decisions and achieve goals and objectives at Store Level.  Key responsibilities include delivering the Perfect Store, executing Account Headquarter plans, and delivering seasonal sell thru objectives and company priorities by identifying incremental selling opportunities for categories under your responsibility.
The primary role of the Retail Sales Manager (RSM) is to leverage data and insights to sell and execute company strategies and priorities by achieving Sales KPI objectives and creating best in class in-store conditions to engage consumers and drive consumption.  The expectation is that RSM will command strong knowledge of the category, shopper trends and consumer usage occasions enabling them to effectively sell incremental assortment and in-store solutions.
As an entry point into our MARS Sales organization, RSM is responsible for building strong customer relationships and collaborating across the Sales functions to identify and resolve operational issues.
The position requires a high degree of integrity with the ability to work efficiently and effectively in an independent fashion without direct supervision.  This position is field based within a defined geography and reports directly to a Retail Sales Lead.
Key Responsibilities:
Build and maintain long-term, trusted relationships with customers by demonstrating strong consultative selling skills to drive sales, retailer profit, ROI, and market share.
Create value by delivering customized sales presentation(s) based on retailer opportunities and priorities to sell incremental orders and mutually beneficial in-store solutions.
Monitor and analyze performance metrics to identify and execute solutions to achieve territory and region KPIs, retailer category growth, and account/company business targets.
Leverage data and demonstrate a strong priority setting to deliver channel/retailer specific seasonal and limited time offer to sell through targets.
Serve as a primary point of contact for customers, ensuring clear communication of sales priorities, orders, and promotional plans.
Position yourself to be a trusted expert, asking open-ended questions and tailoring solutions to specific needs.
Influence merchandising and operational resources to ensure instore excellence, compliance with execution standards, and timely implementation of sales initiatives.  These include assortment priorities (core and innovation), shelving objectives and planogram integrity, as well as incremental semi-permanent and temporary displays.
Responsible and trusted use of technology is essential, including accurate data entry, analysis of sales data to build a selling story, and effective utilization of company systems to support decision-making and performance tracking.
May have Compression call responsibilities. Comfortable preparing and selling to Market Managers, District Mangers depending on customer base of your territory.
Direct 3rd party providers (where applicable) for in-store execution (including seasonal surge).
Where applicable, sell throughout the year by providing business updates to the store's decision maker and contracts which will support delivery of the distribution, shelving, and display objectives.  Enforce compliance.
Maintain high on shelf availability by working with KDM to address inventory discrepancies and order fulfillment.
Participate in team conference calls, training, and attend all sales meetings.
Responsible for storage facility and managing product rotation, inventory allocation, supplies, etc., in an efficient and effective way.

Demonstrate ability to work remotely

Microsoft is a company where passionate innovators come to collaborate, envision what can be and take their careers further. This is a world of more possibilities, more innovation, more openness, and the sky is the limit thinking in a cloud-enabled world.
Microsoft’s Azure Data engineering team is leading the transformation of analytics in the world of data with products like databases, data integration, big data analytics, messaging & real-time analytics, and business intelligence. The products our portfolio include Microsoft Fabric, Azure SQL DB, Azure Cosmos DB, Azure PostgreSQL, Azure Data Factory, Azure Synapse Analytics, Azure Service Bus, Azure Event Grid, and Power BI. Our mission is to build the data platform of AI, powering a new class of data-first applications and driving a data culture.
Within Microsoft Fabric, the Platform team builds and operates the unified foundation that brings together all Fabric workloads into a single, cohesive experience. The platform provides shared infrastructure, governance, security, and a unified data model that enables customers to manage their entire data estate in one place. This team is central to delivering Fabric as a complete, end-to-end intelligence platform.
Every AI agent is only as good as the data it can reach. As a Software Engineer II on the OneLake team, you'll build the highly scalable systems that connect AI to data across clouds, platforms and formats.
OneLake is the open data lake at the heart of Microsoft Fabric and the data foundation for the AI agents built on it. Enterprise data rarely lives in one place. Our team brings it together without copying it: with shortcuts, mirroring and catalog federation, data in Azure, AWS, Google Cloud, Databricks and on-premises systems shows up in OneLake as a single copy, ready for Spark, SQL, Power BI and AI. And the scale is real: OneLake handles over 110 billion interactions a day, more than 15 million shortcuts are in active use, and storage has grown over 300% in a year.

You'll own real services end to end, from design and code to performance and live operations, working alongside experienced engineers who will invest in your growth. location: Orlando, Florida
description: About Rivian Rivian is on a mission to keep the world adventurous forever. Role Summary This position is tailored for an experienced, high-level Senior Field Service Technician who will serve as a technical expert and leader in supporting complex vehicle repairs and field operations. The role requires an adaptable, team-oriented leader capable of driving continuous improvement, mentoring junior team members, and tackling complex diagnostic challenges in a fast-paced environment. While based primarily at a service center, this role may involve operating remotely, traveling to remote locations, or working at production plants to provide advanced field support as business needs demand. Candidates will be evaluated against a comprehensive spectrum of advanced technical skills and leadership capabilities. The schedule for this position will be Tuesday through Saturday 5:00pm - 2:00am This position comes with a 15% pay differential that occurs between 6pm - 6am Responsibilities Advanced Diagnostics & Complex Repairs: Perform bumper-to-bumper diagnostics, complex repairs, installations, and inspections on vehicles both inside service centers and in field settings (customer sites, mobile routes, or remote locations). Technical Support & Remote Troubleshooting: Provide high-level diagnostic guidance to field service teams and perform remote diagnostics or repairs for issues that can be safely addressed without local vehicle access by evaluating logged vehicle data and technical schematics. Leadership & Mentorship: Coach, mentor, and train junior technicians and internal partners; foster cross-functional collaboration and lead shop-floor technical problem-solving. Advanced Tools & Methodologies: Utilize specialized diagnostic tools (e.g., PICO-Scope, PCAN, Kavaser Memorator, breakout boxes) to resolve complex electrical, high-voltage, and network faults. Quality & Process Standardization: Conduct thorough road tests to verify repair quality, champion continuous improvement processes, and drive high standards across repair workflows. Parts Operations & Systems: Oversee complex parts operations—including ordering, receiving, inventory management, and billing—to ensure quality and operational efficiency. Documentation & Technical Feedback: Produce high-quality documentation in service support and engineering systems; provide root-cause analysis and actionable feedback to field service engineers and leadership. Qualifications High School Diploma, GED, or recognized equivalency credential preferred. Graduation from an accredited automotive repair school or vocational program preferred. Minimum age of 21 years old. Valid driver’s license with a clean driving record (no suspensions or revocations within the past 3–5 years). Ability to drive a non-commercial truck and trailer preferred. Availability for a standard 40-hour workweek, including weekends, holidays, early morning, evening, or overnight shifts as required. Ability to travel to regional locations or production plants as needed. Proficient in Windows/Mac environments, work order management systems, and specialized engineering/diagnostic documentation systems. Physical capability to perform occupational tasks (sitting, standing, bending, kneeling, and lifting up to 50 lbs). description: About Rivian Rivian is on a mission to keep the world adventurous forever. Role Summary Rivian's Enterprise Technology (ET) team is moving to an operating model where functional domains own demand and product priorities, a central Software Factory builds and runs custom software, and shared platform teams provide data, AI, and infrastructure. ET Program Management sits between these groups. It leads strategic initiatives that span domains and coordinates plans, dependencies, milestones, risks, and leadership decisions, and it facilitates prioritization against shared delivery capacity. As a Staff Program Manager, you will lead some of ET's largest and most complex cross-functional programs across all the company. You will work with domain leaders, engineering and platform leaders, Finance, and business partners, and in some cases external partners and joint-venture counterparts, to turn competing priorities into clear plans, decisions, and results. You will also use AI tools in your own work and help the team build them into how programs are planned, run, and reported, so that program management at Rivian becomes faster, more consistent, and more data-driven. You will be a strong fit if you have led large, ambiguous, multi-team technology programs, if you can hold your ground with senior leaders while keeping relationships strong, and if you enjoy making a team and a portfolio run better. Responsibilities Strategic program leadership Lead assigned strategic programs end to end across multiple ET domains (for example enterprise applications, software engineering, data and AI, infrastructure, and factory technology), from intake and business case through delivery and handoff. Define scope, deliverables, milestones, success measures, and the critical path, and keep integrated plans current across many teams and vendors. Identify and manage dependencies across domains, including shared capacity, platform readiness, and sequencing, and surface conflicts early with clear options and recommendations. Track risks, issues, and decisions, and drive resolution. Escalate promptly, and prepare leaders for decisions with concise, accurate information. Provide executive-level status and KPI reporting, with a regular cadence for stakeholders, sponsors, and ET leadership. Hand off completed work and documentation to the owning operations teams. Cross-functional prioritization and planning Support the quarterly planning and prioritization process by consolidating demand across functions, mapping it against shared engineering and platform capacity, and preparing the tradeoffs for the joint business and ET leadership forum. Help define and operate the rules that make the process work, such as commitment horizons, how urgent exceptions are handled, and how delivery performance feeds back into the next quarter's capacity decisions. Partner with product owners and functional leads, who own demand and priorities, so that program plans reflect agreed priorities rather than competing ones. Stakeholder and partner management Build trusted relationships with directors and senior leaders across ET and the business, and with Finance, Procurement, Security, and Legal where programs require them. Manage executive and external stakeholders, including vendors and joint-venture partners, and negotiate scope, timing, and resourcing where needed. Push back constructively on unreasonable asks, and align stakeholders with competing priorities on a path forward. Financial and vendor stewardship Own the budget for assigned programs (allocated, spent, and remaining), and keep it reconciled with the ET budget in partnership with the ET budget and Finance owners. Support forecast cycles and variance tracking for program spend, and explain tradeoffs to leaders. Work with Procurement and Finance on vendor, software, and services decisions that affect program scope and cost. Program management capability and standards Work with architecture and engineering leaders so that programs account for the technical constraints and interdependencies that affect delivery. Technical decisions remain with the accountable engineering and architecture owners. Look for ways to simplify, automate, and standardize recurring reporting and program processes. AI-enabled program delivery Use approved AI tools in day-to-day program work, for example to draft and summarize status updates, meeting notes, decision logs, and executive communications, to analyze plans, risks, and dependencies, and to prepare planning and budget materials. Identify where AI and automation can remove manual effort or improve quality in program management workflows (such as intake, status reporting, risk and dependency tracking, and forecast and variance commentary), and design, pilot, and measure those changes. Build repeatable AI-assisted workflows, prompts, templates, and playbooks that other program managers can adopt, and document how and when to use them. Review AI output for accuracy before it is shared, and follow Rivian's guidance on data handling, security, and approved tools. Share effective and responsible AI practices with program managers and stakeholders. Partner with ET's AI, data, and platform teams so that program workflows use enterprise-supported tools and align with ET's AI direction. Qualifications Required Bachelor's degree in business, information systems, computer science, engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. 8 to 12 years of program or project management experience, including leading large or complex cross-functional technology programs with multiple stakeholders, independently. Demonstrated experience managing timelines, resources, budgets, and dependencies across many teams and several domains at once. Enough technical understanding of enterprise systems, software delivery, data, and infrastructure to have meaningful conversations with engineers and to judge risk and feasibility. Proven ability to manage senior stakeholders, including executives and external partners, and to negotiate and push back when needed. Strong written and verbal communication, including clear executive-level status, decision, and risk communication. Experience proactively identifying risks, resolving issues, and suggesting workarounds. Experience mentoring other program managers or improving team processes. Hands-on proficiency with AI tools (for example AI assistants and agents) in a professional setting, and a track record of applying them to improve how work gets done, with sound judgment about accuracy, confidentiality, and when human review is required. Proficiency with Jira, Confluence, or comparable program management tools. Ability to work on-site in Atlanta, GA. Preferred Experience in automotive, manufacturing, or another industry with both enterprise systems and plant or operational technology. Experience with ERP, PLM, or large SaaS implementations, platform consolidations, or build-versus-buy transitions. Experience with portfolio or capacity-based prioritization and planning. Experience partnering with Finance on IT budgets and forecast cycles. Experience working with joint-venture or other external partner organizations. Experience designing, piloting, or scaling AI-assisted or automated workflows for a team (for example prompt libraries, templates, or agent and automation setups), and measuring the effect on speed, quality, or cost. Experience delivering or supporting AI-related programs or platform rollouts. PMP, PgMP, Agile, or similar certification. Familiarity with Google Workspace. Join Our Team as a Machinist!
The Punch Press Machinist is responsible for operating a variety of Punch Press machines, and manually-controlled equipment, to produce precision parts for S&C products. The Machinist interprets blueprints in order to determine part specifications and uses various machines to craft them. They also complete basic documentation and maintenance tasks to ensure processes run smoothly and move materials when needed.
Key Responsibilities
Operate various manual and Punch Press machines (metal forming, tool and die set-up) to fabricate parts according to standard specifications.
Set up machines with the appropriate materials needed to complete the job.
Interpret blueprints, drawings, and other technical specifications to understand the requirements for basic parts and ensure accurate fabrication.
Perform basic routine maintenance on machines and tools to ensure longevity and quality fabrication, including cleaning and reporting mechanical/electrical issues to department leaders.
Utilize an overhead crane and other material handling equipment to safely position materials for machining.
Complete the first-piece inspection of parts using various measurement tools, confirming that the pieces are the correct material, quality, and specifications before beginning the machining process.
Maintain accurate records of fabrication activities, including tracking the progress of job orders and documenting corrective action needed for the machine, part, or process.
Deburr metal parts using hand and/or power tools, ensuring materials are safe to handle and are in a state that’s ready for further processing.
Mentors basic-level team members in the completion of their work to help their professional growth.
Meet department targets and consistently adhere to quality and safety standards.
Understand and comply with all applicable Company policies and rules.
Additional Functions:
Work with departmental mentors to gain and apply feedback in pursuit of improved work quality and accuracy.
Maintain regular and punctual attendance and adherence to policy.
Communicate effectively and respectfully with others.
Attend in-person or virtual meetings as requested or required.
Other responsibilities as assigned.
Maintain ongoing training requirements.
Flexibility to work overtime when required and as scheduled by management
What you’ll Need To Succeed:
High School diploma/GED
2+ years of hands-on experience operating Punch Press machines
Ability to use hand tools and precision measuring instruments such as scales and calipers.
Good knowledge of machine controls and programs with the ability to setup machines to operate new jobs to specific specifications.
Ability to read blueprints
Ability to work independently and meet requirements of assigned materials requests.
Good communication skills (written and verbal) with the ability to articulate information efficiently and effectively to team members in a variety of production support departments.
Basic computer skills with the ability to review and respond to requests via internal applications.
Basic math skills with the ability to calculate quantities, weights, and measurements.
Good interpersonal and organizational skills with the ability to understand and complete requests given by team member inside and outside of the department.
Ability and willingness to follow Health Safety & Environment procedures accurately, reporting concerns promptly to the safety action team.
Preferred:
1+ year of demonstrated experience with the operation of manual and cutting, and punch press (metal forming) machines.

Standing: Most tasks are performed in a standing position with intermittent walking.

Pulling: Occasional use of electric hand truck to move parts a moderate distance.

title: Staff Hardware Test & Validation Lead (On-site)
location: Glen Cove, NY
description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

Standard Bots is America's largest manufacturer of AI-native industrial robots, shipping at scale to customers ranging from small manufacturers to some of the largest companies in the country. We're hiring a technical lead to build and run a central hardware testing function to support product development across the company. You'll set and maintain a high bar for product quality, plan and resource test work, build and run setups from quick bench rigs to long-running validation at scale, and help the team troubleshoot and root-cause failures. The work covers robotic and electromechanical systems of all kinds. Hands-on IC technical lead role, working closely with the mechanical, electrical, and software engineering teams.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

Test Process and Quality Standards. Guide and build a test and validation team, working closely with the hardware team. Standardize how hardware product validation is planned and run, and work with the hardware team to set quality standards. Help turn requirements and specs into test plans.

Planning and Scheduling. Plan and schedule test work and assign lab space, equipment, and people to it. Work closely with hardware and software teams on priorities and timing.

Testbeds, Fixtures, and Ad-Hoc Testing. Help review, design and build complex testbeds and fixtures, including mechanical design, instrumentation, and data acquisition. Run one-off tests from a spec or setup the hardware team provides, and scale them up when needed.

Product Validation and Long-Running Tests. Stand up and run product validation testing across many units, from component qualification to system-level performance tests. Define stop conditions, data products, and post-run inspection, and keep long tests running.

Documentation and Analysis. Strong documentation is a core skill for this role. Write test reports and analysis, procedures, and initial failure analysis. Keep documentation accurate and up to date.

Troubleshooting and Root Cause. Help mechanical and electrical engineers analyze complex failures and perform maintenance to keep hardware running. Engage with engineering teams to respond to and resolve failures.


TOOLS

Sensors and sensing (encoders, IMUs, accelerometers, image processing), data loggers & data collection interfaces, SolidWorks & PDM, oscilloscopes, thermal instrumentation, programming for data processing and analysis, Claude Code (or similar AI tools), typical business and productivity tools (Notion, Asana, Google Docs).


WHAT WE NEED


REQUIRED

 - BS in ME, EE, or similar (or equivalent experience)

 - 5+ years in hardware testing or validation, ideally in robotics, automotive, aerospace, medical, or a similar regulated or safety-critical domain

 - Experience taking complex validation plans from system requirements through test design, execution, and reporting

 - Experience leading and organizing test work, including planning, prioritizing, and assigning lab resources and people

 - Experience with root-cause investigations across ME / EE / FW boundaries

 - Comfortable writing test plans with clear pass/fail criteria and choosing sample sizes based on confidence needs

 - Hands-on with electrical instrumentation (scopes, probes, etc.) and reading schematics

 - Mechanical fundamentals including tolerance stacks, motor analysis, power transmission, bearings, fits, and structural design

 - Strong written documentation habits and experience


NICE TO HAVE

 - Collaborative or industrial robots, or 6-DOF motion systems

 - Functional safety standards: ISO 13849, ISO 10218, IEC 61508, or ISO 26262

 - Mechanical / electrical design of fixtures and tooling

 - DFMEA / PFMEA or formal reliability practices

 - Failure analysis and root-cause analysis


WHERE THE ROLE GROWS

Over time, the role can expand to include:

 - Cross-Platform Test Strategy: own test strategy across platforms and set common test methods for every program

 - Lab Capability and Infrastructure: expand testing range and scope, plus test automation, fleet monitoring, and supporting infrastructure

 - Reliability Program: track MTBF / B-life and feed corrective actions back to design

 - Phase Gates and Design Reviews: represent testing at EVT/DVT/PVT gates and in DFMEA/PFMEA reviews

 - Technical Mentorship: mentor test engineers and technicians as the group grows

Compensation and Benefits:

The base salary range for this role is $160,000 to $200,000, depending on experience. Base salary is just one part of the overall compensation at Standard Bots. All Full-Time Employees are eligible for Employee Stock Options. We also offer a package of benefits including paid time off, medical/dental/vision insurance, life insurance, disability insurance, and 401(k) to regular full-time employees.

The Batch Compute Experience team owns the platform that Stripe engineers use to build, run, debug and optimize Apache Spark jobs. Those jobs handle large-scale data processing for analytics, machine learning, finance and core product data pipelines. Hundreds of engineers and thousands of production jobs driving critical business processes, such as payouts and reconciliations, run on this platform.
Today, diagnosing and tuning a job means reasoning by hand across scattered telemetry, configuration, query plans and application code. Our goal is to make Spark at Stripe fast to iterate, reliable by default, and self-optimizing, so engineers can focus on business logic instead of Spark internals. We're doing this through three connected efforts:
Modernization : keeping Stripe's Spark runtime and dependency stack current, including Spark 3.5 → Spark 4, Scala 2.13 and Apache Iceberg. We're building automated upgrade and validation tools so that upgrading the whole fleet becomes routine and low-risk instead of a multi-year manual effort
Agentic Spark and optimization : building trustworthy, AI-powered workflows that diagnose failed or underperforming jobs, recommend fixes based on evidence, and carry them safely into configuration changes, code PRs or escalations. We also want to optimize configuration, query plans and code across the whole fleet
Operational excellence : making the platform reliable, observable and compliant, and defining user-experience metrics that show whether we're succeeding
Over the longer term, we want to turn the platform into a Spark control plane that keeps learning. It should detect problems before users notice them, validate fixes safely and apply them through policy-controlled automation.

As a Staff Engineer on Batch Compute Experience, you'll set the technical direction for one of Stripe's most widely used data platforms. Lead Spark modernization across the fleet. Own the technical strategy for moving thousands of production jobs to newer Spark and Iceberg runtimes. Make upgrades continuous and safe. Design and evolve automated upgrade and validation systems: shadow execution against production data, output-correctness comparison, sandboxed execution, and staged promotion. The goal is to make each new runtime upgrade cheaper than the last

As a Mechanic on Via's Operations team, you'll be hands-on every day - diagnosing, repairing, and maintaining the buses and support vehicles that keep our transit service running. This is a technical, floor-focused role for someone who takes pride in getting under the hood, solving problems the right way the first time, and keeping a fleet on the road safely and reliably.
This is an in-person position with the expectation that you will be on-site 5 days per week out of our Elmira (Chemung County), New York location. What You'll Do:
Perform routine preventive maintenance on electric vehicles & transit vehicles, and support equipment, including fluid changes, filter replacements, brake inspections, tire rotations, and scheduled service intervals
Diagnose and repair mechanical, electrical, and hydraulic issues across engines, transmissions, braking systems, HVAC, suspension, steering, and electrical systems.

Respond to road calls and in-service breakdowns, troubleshooting issues on-site and coordinating with the Maintenance Manager to minimize service disruption.
Use automotive test equipment, diagnostic software, and manufacturer diagrams to isolate issues and verify repairs.

Keep the shop and work areas clean, organized, and safe: tools returned, fluids stored properly, and hazards addressed before they become issues.

Hands-on problem solver who enjoys working on the floor, not behind a desk.
Comfortable reading schematics, wiring diagrams, and technical manuals.
Proficient with diagnostic tools and comfortable learning new maintenance software.

Comfortable with physical work, including lifting, bending, standing for extended periods, and working in varied shop conditions.

Hold a high school diploma or GED certificate.

At least 21 years old.
Successful completion of mandatory pre-employment drug test, criminal background check, and motor vehicle records check.

The Digital Process & Work Standards Product Manager is responsible for creating and maintaining a consistent, simplified way of working across Truck Service, from intake through closeout.

Key Responsibilities
Process Architecture
Own current-state ShopCore and future-state D365 Field Service workflows from intake through closeout.
Define roles, decision points, exceptions, controls, and handoffs across end-to-end processes.
Simplify and standardize processes before automation or digitization.
Maintain integrated process maps and ensure workflows remain aligned across products and functions.
Identify process gaps, inefficiencies, and opportunities for simplification and standardization.
Standard Jobs, Work Standards & External Data
Govern standard-job scope, labor requirements, inspections, parts expectations, and completion criteria.
Own change control and versioning for standard jobs and related work standards.
Define how external data sources, including MOTOR Standard Repair Times, are used and maintained.
Ensure labor and job standards remain accurate, controlled, and current.
Establish governance practices that support consistent application of standards across Truck Service.

Lead cross-functional integration and dependency reviews.
Maintain an integrated process map and decision log.
Resolve conflicting requirements, terminology, and dependencies across different products and functions.
